must_remember: Absolute zero is defined as $0\text{ K}$, which corresponds to $-273.15^{\circ}\text{C}$.
The thermodynamic Kelvin scale is independent of the thermometric properties of any particular substance.
The triple point of water is defined as exactly $273.16\text{ K}$ where ice, liquid water, and water vapor coexist.
According to kinetic theory, the average translational kinetic energy per molecule is given by $\langle E \rangle = \frac{3}{2}k_B T$.
In the 2019 SI redefinition, the Kelvin is fixed by assigning an exact numerical value to the Boltzmann constant $k_B$.

glossary.meaning: Temperature measured on the Kelvin scale starting from absolute zero ($0\text{ K}$).
The unique temperature ($273.16\text{ K}$) and pressure at which ice, liquid water, and water vapor are in equilibrium.
The maximum theoretical efficiency of a heat engine operating between two absolute temperatures $T_C$ and $T_H$, given by $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$.
The lowest possible energy that a quantum mechanical physical system may possess, remaining present even at absolute zero ($0\text{ K}$).
